share.title: Knesset Vote Match
share.text: Which lists vote the way you would? A quiz on the record of the Knesset, for the election of 27 October 2026:

sections.title: Where a list's position comes from.
sections.text: Only from what its candidates who were members of the Knesset did in the 24th–25th Knesset:

bullets.text: A sponsored bill counts {vote_ratio} times more than a vote: pushing for a change is louder than voting against one.
Private and government bills, except budget laws: a vote on the whole budget says nothing about its separate articles.

bullets.lead: Promises and speeches are not used.
bullets.text: Only the Knesset record.
The Knesset's open database and the Central Elections Committee's candidate lists.

sections.title: Whose record a list carries.
sections.text: Its candidates who were members of the Knesset — and only they.

bullets.text: The partners' former members are counted together; a partner with more of them weighs more.
Their record goes with them.

bullets.lead: How many former members it takes.
bullets.text: A list is ranked from {min_ex_mks} former members; with one, it is shown but not ranked.

sections.title: Which lists have a record.
sections.text: Only the Knesset record of former members (24th–25th Knesset) is used. New candidates and platforms are not seen.

bullets.text: can be evaluated.
{single?is|are} shown but not ranked.

sections.title: Lists without a record.
sections.text: {no_record} {no_record?list has|lists have} no record in the Knesset and {no_record?is|are} not shown in the results:

bullets.text: Strength matters only when your answers are mixed.
Lists with extreme positions come out on top a little more often.
The list's record on this statement is too weak to call a side, or rests on one former member or one bill.
The position rests on very few people.

bullets.lead: “Position known for only N% of your answers”.
bullets.text: The list has a position on less than half of your answers: shown below the others, not ranked.
They never leave your device. The site counts only how many people start the quiz and how many reach the results — nothing else is sent.

sections.title: The order of questions.
sections.text: {core} statements are the same for everyone, then {clarify} are chosen for you.

bullets.text: The questions that best separate the lists.
Chosen one at a time to tell apart the lists closest to you so far.
Topics most voters care about come first; this changes only which questions you see, not how your answers count.

sections.title: Limitations — what this quiz can and cannot tell you.
sections.text: The quiz is an orientation, not a precise measurement.

bullets.lead: Ministers and prime ministers sponsor few bills.
bullets.text: A list led by them is measured mostly by its other former members and by votes.
About 98 % of votes in the Knesset follow the member's bloc, so a vote is partly discipline.

bullets.lead: Topic labels were made by a language model
bullets.text: and checked by other models: on a random sample, the topic was right in about 86 % of cases and the side in about 98 %. Individual mistakes remain.

bullets.lead: Checks so far were done by models, not by people.
bullets.text: Agreement between models is not accuracy for real voters.
Lists with close values cannot be told apart: read them as «about as close».
(«even if …») is not measured.

bullets.lead: A vote against a bill can hide the opposite reason.
bullets.text: A party may oppose a draft for being too soft.

sections.title: How topics are chosen.
sections.text: A topic gets a statement only if the lists' former members acted differently on it in the Knesset:

bullets.text: At least {min_lists} evaluated lists with a position on the topic, each resting on {min_mks} or more former members.
Their positions spread by at least {min_spread}.
At least {min_names} distinct bills sponsored by them; a re-submitted bill counts once.
Chosen by testing which values held between the 24th and 25th Knesset, frozen on 18 October 2026, the same for every topic.
A bill shared by a topic and a broader one counts toward only one of them.

sections.after: Topics where all lists pushed the same way, or with too few bills, are left out — even when important.

sections.title: Important topics that are not in the quiz, and why

bullets.lead: The lists' records hardly differ — nearly everyone pushed the same way:
bullets.text: relief for war and terror victims; support for families with children; credit and mortgages; tax enforcement; support for charities; banning harmful online and broadcast content.

bullets.lead: Too few lists have a record once budget votes are set aside:
bullets.text: the power of labor unions; defamation law; assisted reproduction.

bullets.lead: Too few bills by the candidates to place the lists:
bullets.text: abortion; who is registered as a Jew; the Law of Return for grandchildren of Jews; gun licensing; immunity for soldiers; laws tied to a state of emergency; the Yemenite children affair; the autonomy of minors; cameras in kindergartens and institutions; the term of Supreme Court justices; sports on free channels.

selecting judges (in «Politicians' influence over the courts»); the weight of the Attorney General (in «Ministers' control over senior officials»); civil marriage and divorce (in «Civil marriage» and «Divorce»); conditions on funding religious schools (in «Funding schools without the core curriculum»); alternatives to military service (in «Drafting yeshiva students»); international law and UNRWA (in «Foreign states and international organizations in Israel»); the death penalty and sanctions on terrorists' families (in «Counter-terrorism measures»); judicial review of government decisions (in «Overriding court rulings»); preferences for underrepresented groups (in «Benefits for those who served»); surveillance powers of the security services (in «Protection of personal data»); bank fees and duties (in «Protecting the weaker party to a contract»); local preference in government purchasing (the mirror of «Imports and competition»).

bullets.lead: Bills on unrelated subjects, no single honest question:
bullets.text: bans on publishing victims' details; state ownership of disputed property; co-owners' rights in apartment buildings; accountability of individual officials; criminal liability of officials for abuse of office.

bullets.lead: Administrative matters with no position a voter would hold:
bullets.text: licensing procedures for businesses and professions; terms and deadlines; the size of public bodies; inheritance law; state awards.

sections.after: Not present at all, because no bill of a former member of the Knesset carries the topic in a way that separates the lists: the Gaza war and the hostages, a Palestinian state, the cost of living as such. The quiz measures legislation, not campaigns.
